check: Frontmatter holds no multi-line YAML block (`|`, `>`): git ls-files '*SKILL.md' '*/commands/*.md' '*/agents/*.md' | xargs awk 'FNR==1{fm=($0=="---")} FNR>1&&fm&&$0=="---"{fm=0} fm&&/^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*[|>][-+0-9]*[[:space:]]*$/{print FILENAME": "$0; bad=1} END{exit bad}'

A skill's description is one line of at most 1024 characters: git ls-files '*SKILL.md' | xargs awk 'FNR==1{fm=($0=="---")} FNR>1&&fm&&$0=="---"{fm=0} FNR==1{d=0} fm&&/^description:/{d=1; v=substr($0,14); sub(/^ +/,"",v); if(v==""||length(v)>1024){print FILENAME": description empty or over 1024"; bad=1}; next} fm&&d&&/^[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]/{print FILENAME": description runs past one line"; bad=1} fm&&!/^[[:space:]]/{d=0} END{exit bad}'
No `when_to_use` key in skill frontmatter: git ls-files '*SKILL.md' | xargs awk 'FNR==1{fm=($0=="---")} FNR>1&&fm&&$0=="---"{fm=0} fm&&/^when_to_use:/{print FILENAME; bad=1} END{exit bad}'

Version lives in plugin.json only, never in SKILL.md frontmatter: git ls-files '*SKILL.md' | xargs awk 'FNR==1{fm=($0=="---")} FNR>1&&fm&&$0=="---"{fm=0} fm&&/^version:/{print FILENAME; bad=1} END{exit bad}'

A skill that stays in this repo is marked internal in its metadata: for f in $(git ls-files '.claude/skills/*SKILL.md'); do awk 'FNR==1{fm=($0=="---")} FNR>1&&fm&&$0=="---"{fm=0} fm&&/^metadata:/{m=1;next} fm&&m&&/^[[:space:]]+internal:[[:space:]]*true[[:space:]]*$/{ok=1} fm&&!/^[[:space:]]/{m=0} END{exit !ok}' "$f" || { echo "not internal: $f"; exit 1; }; done

Scripts hold no Windows paths: ! git ls-files '*.sh' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.js' '*.mjs' | grep -v /vendor/ | xargs grep -nE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9])[A-Za-z]:(\\+|/[A-Za-z])|(^|[[:space:]"'\''=(])\.{1,2}\\+[A-Za-z]|%(USERPROFILE|APPDATA|LOCALAPPDATA|HOMEPATH)%'

Every plugin is listed in the marketplace: for d in $(git ls-files '*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json' | sed 's#/.claude-plugin/plugin.json##'); do jq -e --arg s "./$d" 'any(.plugins[]; .source == $s)' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json >/dev/null || { echo "unlisted: $d"; exit 1; }; done

Claude Code validates the marketplace and each listed plugin, one hooks module per plugin included: claude plugin validate . && for p in $(jq -r '.plugins[].source' .claude-plugin/marketplace.json); do claude plugin validate "$p" || exit 1; done

Every hook is a function hook, so no hooks.json or plugin.json has a `hooks` key: for f in $(git ls-files '*/hooks/hooks.json' '*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json'); do jq -e 'has("hooks")|not' "$f" >/dev/null || { echo "command hooks: $f"; exit 1; }; done
Every hunch skill has a HYPOTHESIS.md: for d in hunch/skills/*/; do [ -f "$d/HYPOTHESIS.md" ] || { echo "no HYPOTHESIS.md: $d"; exit 1; }; done
hunch's version stays 0.x: jq -e '.version | startswith("0.")' hunch/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
The worker's specs pass: cd factory && bun test
Each plugin's hook tests pass: for p in $(git ls-files '*/hooks/hooks.json' | cut -d/ -f1); do claude plugin test "$p" || exit 1; done
factory's lint passes: cd factory && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun run lint
Every tracked shell test passes: git ls-files '*.test.sh' | while read -r t; do bash "$t" || exit 1; done
plan: A model-judgment boundary (a judge, a generated artifact, an LLM check) gets a deterministic fence where one exists, and a measured pass-rate on a labeled set before anyone trusts it.
No work-state file only the agent reads (.jsonl, workflow-state.json).
Rebuild nothing Claude Code already ships and turns on; compete on thinking quality.
No parallel agent sessions beyond what the human can attend to.
Never trade human comprehension for output volume, and never automate friction that builds understanding.
A change goes in the plugin whose role in PHILOSOPHY.md fits it.
Pick each new unit by moo-authoring's unit choice table: runtime file, skill, human-only skill, function hook, hunch skill with HYPOTHESIS.md, or repo-local skill.
Before building a unit, count how often its situation occurs in real session transcripts, and weigh each case by what the miss cost.
A new skill only when the kind of thinking changes: one skill, one mode, one gate. Two skills over one when their triggers differ.
Content for one branch of a skill goes in a file the skill opens on that branch, named where it is needed.
A pane or band is verified on events copied from real session transcripts, one per shape it renders.
Prior art first: search libraries, then the codebase, before building.
Define what must NOT happen before what should.
When options conflict, take the one with fewer moving parts.
judge: Every change serves at least one of moo's four outcomes: less decision regret, more conceptual clarity, fewer but stronger artifacts, the capacity to own what you produce.
A skill's description carries what makes it fire; its body carries the procedure. A `disable-model-invocation: true` skill's description sums up its invocation for the human.
A hook fails open: on any error it passes the event on and shows the failure once, as a toast.
No claim that a model-judgment boundary works from one run, and no model of its failures as a finite set already handled.
No reference chain: a file whose content is a pointer to another file.
No wall-clock estimate of the agent's own work, except where a human watches a live surface and needs it to tell working from wedged.
No content duplicated across docs; link to the one source. Two copies may stand only across a compaction boundary.
No inline example that narrows the exploration space; a case that fixes a term's meaning or marks where a property stops holding is fine.
No catalog of what the harness already lists, such as tool indexes or skill tables.
No cargo-cult process step: every step has a reason.
A condition that follows what a skill does reads `Use when <condition>.`, a finite clause.
A skill is sized by a deletion pass, never a numeric cap.
Decision tables over prose explanations; bullets for lists, a paragraph for one connected argument.
Every sentence passes "does Claude need this?"; no vague terms, one term per concept.
Design decisions read "X over Y: reason".
Skills compose by name: a body invokes a sibling with the Skill tool, never copies in its body, and names a sibling only in a refusal or a route.
A finished run states what is settled and what is open in its own words, never who handles it next.
A skill's output is bounded by what it hands back: a restatement as short as it goes, the user's own words preserved, a structure bounded part by part; no line cap on a handed-back artifact.
A hook never starts a turn the human didn't ask for: no wake, no `$.prompt.submit` of its own. It hands to Claude only on the human's Enter, through `$.prompt.fill`.
What a hook finds waits in the band above the prompt, only while it holds something; detail unfolds on a press and folds back.
Hook work longer than one dispatch runs unawaited, so the turn's end is never held.
Hook state lives in `$.state` (this session) or `$.store` (across sessions), never in temp files or module variables: a hot reload drops module variables.
A hook that spawns headless `claude -p` copies its flag set from `hope/hooks/judge.sh`.
A hope skill body stops when a sibling it names is missing, never degrades.
No rigid frameworks: a skill skips steps that don't apply.
Default to less; expand on request.
A hunch experiment that leans on judgment graduates only with a measured pass-rate, never from one good run.
none: Clarity before action: ask when you would be guessing at what is wanted.
Investigation before implementation: keep find and fix apart where the fix carries a diagnosis.
Retrieved over recalled: look up what can be looked up; exhaust tools before asking humans.
Proven over invented: named frameworks with evidence over novel method.
Adapt to context: session type and engagement level shape behavior.
Presence over velocity: if nothing receives care, stop producing.
Correction is signal: receive a correction; don't defend the old approach.
Cost falls on them: weigh a recommendation knowing the burden lands on the human.
Advise, don't command: disclose uncertainty and explain why.
Own before producing more: understand the current artifact before making the next.
Friction when it teaches: keep friction that builds mental models and shows edge cases.
No ownership without understanding: if you can't explain it, you don't own it.
Exit is honest: at every release each hunch experiment graduates, stays with a stated reason, or dies.
